ar_wizardry_boulders.blurb: Wizardry Boulders is a very small bouldering spot on Fitzgerald Mountain in northwest Arkansas, tucked into the Fitzgerald North section. Five problems are spread over a couple of short blocks beside a mountain-bike trail, with room for a few more just below. Everything is easy, running from V1 up to about V2. Several top-outs finish directly on the trail, so take care landing and topping out. It suits climbers looking for gentle problems, and the surrounding Fitzgerald North zone adds highballs, short easy blocks and a cave or two for a longer session.

ar_upper_fading_light_boulders.blurb: Upper Fading Light Boulders is a cluster of five problems within the Fading Light group, on the east side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas. It collects most of that group's easy lines: three are at the very bottom of the scale and the other two reach V1. Arriving from the Roman Wall, these are the first boulders you pass. The wider Fading Light zone lies beneath the Horseshoe and Hand Grenades area and also holds some harder problems, so this spot works as a gentle starting point for the zone.

ar_5_frontier_wall.blurb: Frontier Wall is the southernmost numbered section of Fitzgerald South on Fitzgerald Mountain in northwest Arkansas. It is a short wall crowned by an overhanging roof, with five sport routes between 5.9 and 5.10, one of which can also be top-roped. Across Fitzgerald South, routes run roughly 25 to 50 feet and are bolted with comfortable spacing for leading. The stone there is hard but can fracture and shed pieces, so a helmet is recommended. The wall sits east of the trail that continues almost to the end of the property.

ar_motivational_wall.blurb: Motivational Wall is a small trad wall at Stack Rock, a remote crag in the Richland Creek area of north-central Arkansas. It holds five gear routes from 5.7 to 5.10, with more face climbing than crack and rock described as high quality. You reach it by branching left from the Wall of Moderates on the way in. Stack Rock as a whole gets both sun and shade through the day, but loose rock is common, and from May through September the trail and crag grow over with briars, ticks, chiggers and snakes.
